# EXP-0004 draft claims (to be refuted)

Data: C:\code\llama.cpp-fork\research\results\experiments\EXP-0004\
  - analyze_timeline.py (the analyzer), aggregate.py, bench_timeline.sh, long_runs.sh
  - timeline_<arm>_t1/_t2.json (128-token runs, two traced reps), timeline_<arm>_long.json (1024-token runs)
  - log_<arm>_*.txt (the app's own stderr: cache counters, eval time, pinning line)
  - decomposition.csv / decomposition.md (aggregate of the 128-token runs)
  - long_runs_windows.json (1024-token runs per 128-token window + Windows paging counters summed over decode / before decode)
  - paging_<arm>_long.csv (typeperf, 1 s), wall_<arm>_long.txt (wall-clock start/end of the nsys launch)
  - device_query.json, code_reading.json (code readers + verifiers), literature.json
Raw captures (sqlite, read-only, CPU-only queries are fine): C:\nsys\exp0004\<tag>.sqlite
Setup: llama-completion, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL, -ngl 99 -ncmoe 40 --moe-cache-mib N, 46-token prompt, greedy,
RTX 4060 Ti PCIe 4.0 x8 under WDDM, 31 GiB host RAM (16.5-18 GiB free), model 20.8 GiB of which 18.3 GiB experts, mmap.
nsys 2025.6.3, --trace=cuda-sw,nvtx --cuda-graph-trace=graph:host-only, no sampling.
Arms: cache 256/586/1024/2048 MiB pageable (default); 1024/2048 with GGML_CUDA_REGISTER_HOST=1 (pins 7842 MiB = 42% of
expert bytes, the default RAM/4 cap; the rest stays pageable).

## Claims

C1. During generation the expert host-to-device copies never overlap GPU compute: overlap measured 0.000 ms/token in all
15 traced captures (12 short + 3 long), consistent with the code (one stream, two full host syncs per MoE layer).

C2. GPU compute (union of CUDA graph spans and kernels) is 12.7-12.9 ms/token in every arm and window, independent of cache
size and pinning. CUDA graphs are used: 41 graph launches per token, ~0 individual kernels in short runs (~6/token in long
runs, from graph rebuilds).

C3. Token time decomposes (128-token fresh-process runs, means of two reps) as e.g. 2048 MiB pageable: 139.6 ms =
compute 12.9 + DMA 26.3 + GPU idle 100.3; of the idle, 91.7 ms is while the host thread is inside expert copies whose host
call runs below 1.5 GB/s ("slow copies"), 4.8 ms in fast-copy staging, 2.2 ms in cudaStreamSynchronize, ~1.6 other.

C4. The slow copies are hard page faults on the mmap'd expert pages: (a) the host-rate distribution is bimodal with a
trough between 1 and 2 GB/s (slow mode ~0.36 GB/s host-side); (b) in the 1024-token runs the bytes of slow copies match
the disk bytes read during decode (6.05 vs 6.19 GiB, 4.62 vs 5.06, 4.49 vs 5.61); (c) counts are deterministic between
reps (6819 vs 6819 etc.) except at 256 MiB, and decay over the run (first-touch); (d) pinned arms fault ~60% as often,
matching the 58% of expert bytes left pageable.

C5. Fresh-process short runs are dominated by first-touch faults: 2048 MiB pageable goes from 118.8 ms/token in the
first 128-token window to 52.1 ms/token in the 7th; slow-copy idle falls from 69.3 to 3.8 ms/token. The OS does not keep
the model cached between back-to-back runs on this host (about 15 GiB read from disk per run).

C6. Warm (tokens 771-898) decomposition: 2048 pageable 52.1 = compute 12.8 + DMA 26.3 + idle 12.9; 586 pageable
74.0 = 12.8 + 42.7 + 18.4; 2048 pinned(42%) 44.5 = 12.8 + 20.3 + 11.3. So once warm, DMA is the largest single component
(50-58%), compute 17-29%, host-side idle 22-25%.

C7. DMA rates: pageable copies whose pages are resident run at 8.6-9.0 GB/s on the GPU side while copying and 7.1-7.6
GB/s host-side; pinned copies run at 12.8 GB/s GPU-side (about 91% of a ~14 GB/s usable PCIe 4.0 x8 link) and return to the
host immediately (~130-140 GB/s apparent). Finding 4's 3.4-5.5 GB/s were bytes divided by whole-token time, and its
statement that compute overlaps the copies is wrong.

C8. Pinning's gain splits into two parts the old throughput sweep could not separate (OPEN_QUESTIONS Q3): in cold windows
mostly fault avoidance (2048, first window: total -23.5 ms, of which slow-copy idle -15.7, DMA -3.8, staging -4.0);
in warm windows mostly DMA rate (last window: total -7.6, DMA -6.0, slow-copy idle -1.5).

C9. Trace completeness: trace-counted expert upload bytes over decode equal the cache's own counter minus exactly
15.5625 MiB in every arm; that is 8 experts x 2,039,808 B of one group-2 layer (layer 39) uploaded through the cache during
the prefill, because output pruning leaves layer 39's FFN with one token. So no copy was dropped by the tracer.

C10. Tracing overhead is small: traced eval ms/token is 1.4-4% below... i.e. untraced is 1.5-4% slower or faster? (check:
untraced eval ms/token vs traced eval ms/token per arm in the logs) and the decomposition is not distorted by it.

C11. Upper bounds for the levers, warm 2048 pageable (52 ms/token): (a) overlap of copy with compute can hide at most
compute = 12.8 ms/token (25%), and without prediction only the shared expert / hit experts / gate-up-while-down-uploads,
tens of microseconds per layer; with next-layer prediction at the literature's 70-90% recall, less than that;
(b) pinning all experts would cut DMA to about 26.3 x 8.6/12.8 = 17.7 ms and remove staging and faults, ~34 ms/token
(+53%), but needs ~18.3 GiB of locked RAM on a 31 GiB host; (c) the per-layer syncs cost ~2 ms/token, small.
Hence the roadmap should put host memory residency/pinning ahead of copy-stream overlap and prediction.

C12. The standing rebase check passed: B1 at 2048 MiB reproduced 61.38% / 58033.62 MiB exactly on 5df437a57.

GPU work from other processes (e.g. the WDDM compositor) is invisible, so 'idle' means idle for this process.

Clock caveat quantified. GPU start minus API start is never negative across 61.8k-747k records per capture (min 5.6-6.4 us). Sync end minus the end of preceding GPU work is never negative across 13.4k-115k syncs (min 1.4-1.9 us). So any CPU/GPU offset lies in [-1.5, +5.6] us. Shifting all GPU timestamps across that range changes the 2048-pageable buckets by at most 0.06 (slow), 0.06 (fast), 0.11 (sync) and 0.08 (no_api) ms/token.

The DMA bucket is clean. For pageable copies the GPU record starts a median 4.7 us after the host call returns (GPU start - API start 87.4 us against host 82.7 us for fast copies; 1655.6 against 1656.0 us for slow), so staging and fault time sit entirely in host/idle time. Only 0.05-0.10% of decode pageable copies have a GPU-side rate below 5 GB/s (<=0.045 ms/token excess). No per-copy GPU rate exceeds 13.33 GB/s, so no record understates its transfer.

Pageable DMA is 37% slower when the host stages the next copy at the same time. In 2048-pageable_t1 the rate is 8.08-9.00 GB/s with concurrent fast staging (>50% of the DMA) against 12.78-12.97 GB/s without; 2048-pinned_t1 gives 8.14 against 13.00. So about a third of pageable 'DMA' time is contention-stretched. This changes why pinning helps in warm windows: removal of staging contention, not a different DMA path.

verdicts.reason: The page-fault mechanism holds up under every alternative I tested. The numbers in (b) and (d) need fixing. (a) The rate histogram is cleanly bimodal: slow peak at 0.32-0.50 GB/s, fast peak at 6-10 GB/s, and only 4-48 copies per bin between 0.63 and 1.58 GB/s. Moving the threshold from 1.0 to 2.0 GB/s changes the slow count by 10137->10182 (+0.4%, 2048-long), 7481->7609 (+1.7%, 586-long) and 6819->6823 (2048_t1). Slow host time changes by under 0.4%. Each slow copy costs a near-constant 174-177 us per 64 KiB (p10 150, p90 203), whatever its size. In decode, Pages Input / Page Reads = 15.4 pages per read, so these are synchronous 64 KiB cluster reads issued one at a time. Slow copies have the same size mix as fast ones (576K/704K/840K = 64/34/2% vs 63/32/5%). Alternatives ruled out: (1) Staging-buffer exhaustion: the GPU is idle for 97-98% of slow-copy host time (17.05 of 17.49 ms/token long; 91.7 of 94.0 short), and the GPU-side DMA of slow copies runs at 9.8 GB/s, so the host is not waiting on DMA. (2) CPU contention, WDDM paging, antivirus: these would be random, but slow positions are identical between reps and between arms, and their bytes track disk reads second by second. (3) Memory compression: no disk reads would result, yet disk reads match. (4) Pinned copies held up behind something: pinned copies return at 130-150 GB/s apparent, and only 1 of ~250k was slow. (b) Using trace-anchored windows (TARGET_INFO_SESSION_START_TIME is wall start + 0.81 s) and binning slow-copy bytes into the same typeperf intervals: 2048-pageable 6.09 vs 6.25 GiB, per-second r=0.999. 2048-pinned 4.68 vs 4.83 GiB, r=0.999. Shifting the window by 1 s moves both sides equally, so the 2048 match is real and not an artifact of window choice. (c) t1 and t2 are slow at the same 6819 of 6819 (token, copy) positions. In tokens 700-1022 of the long runs, the pageable and pinned arms share 533 slow positions. Of the 427 slow only in the pageable run, all 427 are tensors pinned in the pinned run. Only 38 are slow only in the pinned run. So late faults depend on the access history, not on memory pressure, which fits first touch. The 256 MiB arm is the exception: 1636 positions are slow in t2 but fast in t1, although the copy sequences are identical. (d) The pinned/pageable ratio is 59.7% (2048 short), 61.1% (1024 short) and 59.5% (long, tokens 700+). Over the whole long runs it is 76% (7731/10147), because the pageable long run started partly warm.
